cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Change What the Apology Is For
cards.instruction: Get an apology, then reveal that the original offense was only the first layer of what needs repair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. I accept your apology for breaking the vase.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. The vase was cheap. You let me blame the dog for three days.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then tell the dog and me which part of that embarrassment we deserved.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 accepts apology and A3 sets a deeper blame issue, but A5 asks who deserved B embarrassment rather than directing repair of the actual false blame.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 uses B2 replacement offer to distinguish cheap object from concealment; A5 responds to B4 embarrassment with unclear transfer of that feeling.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers replacement and B4 explains concealment plausibly, while A final wording makes the requested repair less clear.

heightening.evidence: A5 does not clearly develop how B should repair blaming the dog; deserved embarrassment shifts the object of injury.

specificity.evidence: A1 vase and A3 three days of dog blame are concrete; A5 pronoun that embarrassment muddies the account.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 dog address could be playable, but its explanatory question is less clear than naming false blame.
